I'll add a new test file that runs the real script against a temp directory. The change is already in the script, so the test will pass immediately. To watch it fail for the right reason, I'll run it once against a copy of the script that still keeps five.

<edit path="tests/test_rotate_logs.py">
import os
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

SCRIPT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "bin" / "rotate-logs.sh"


def test_keeps_the_seven_newest_gz_archives(tmp_path):
    # app-00 is the oldest, app-09 the newest
    for i in range(10):
        archive = tmp_path / f"app-{i:02d}.log.gz"
        archive.write_bytes(b"x")
        os.utime(archive, (1_000_000 + i * 100, 1_000_000 + i * 100))
    notes = tmp_path / "notes.txt"
    notes.write_text("keep me")

    result = subprocess.run(
        ["sh", str(SCRIPT), str(tmp_path)], capture_output=True, text=True
    )

    assert result.returncode == 0
    remaining = sorted(p.name for p in tmp_path.glob("*.gz"))
    assert remaining == [f"app-{i:02d}.log.gz" for i in range(3, 10)]
    assert notes.exists()
</edit>

2. Back up the script and make a temporary copy of the old behavior (keep five, `tail -n +6`) to check the test catches it. This is a mutation check only, and the original is restored right after:
<command>cp bin/rotate-logs.sh /tmp/rotate-logs.sh.bak && sed -i '' 's/+8/+6/' bin/rotate-logs.sh && uv run pytest tests/test_rotate_logs.py -v; cp /tmp/rotate-logs.sh.bak bin/rotate-logs.sh && cat bin/rotate-logs.sh</command>
I expect an assertion failure showing only five archives remaining, not a setup error. The `cat` confirms the script is back to `+8`.

3. Run the project's full suite, since the new test alone isn't a green suite:
<command>uv run pytest -q</command>
